| [TERM-143](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-143.md) v2 | bulk, in two senses that come apart: by count, the many members or directions that make up most of a population or spectrum, and by weight, the few that carry most of its mass, density or activity; in a skewed distribution or spectrum the two sit at opposite ends | At the owner's correction of 2026-11-22, on a relay of Song, Ahn and Yun that used "bulk" for the many low-curvature directions: 'you have my intended meaning of 'bulk' backwards, I meant that in the sense of the domain which carries the dominant density. in the context of e.g. the 80-20 rule, the *bulk* of the population does not contribute the *bulk* of the activity. By count, the bulk is the many: Song et al.'s "bulk subspace", the complement of the top Hessian eigenvectors, and random-matrix theory's continuous bulk of a spectrum, from which outliers detach ([TERM-138](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-138.md), sense 3). By weight, the bulk is the few that carry most of the mass or activity: the owner's sense, the top eigenvalues of an operator. In a skewed population or spectrum the two sit at opposite ends, as the 80-20 rule says and as [CLAIM-832](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-832.md) holds for heavy tails (most events small by count, most of the total in the tail).
